reviews.text:
My mother is well looked after and every staff interaction I have seen has been kind and respectful. The senior nurses are always helpful and knowledgeable about her care.
The management is good with plenty of opportunities to ask questions or voice concerns
reviews.author: Sandra Springall

reviews.text: We had a very positive and caring experience when my mum moved to Westgate. The staff on Glenpark Ward are lovely and although mum arrived at Westgate House Care Home with advanced dementia, her feelings were always taken into consideration when making choices about her. Thanks to all of you for making mum's stay one where she felt safe and loved.
reviews.author: Sylma Laviniere

reviews.text: Horrible. Went to visit my grandma with dementia. She thought I was a worker called John! And told me John had been giving her some pills, she hasn’t been prescribed any pills. But I thought she made it all up. So I left it. She then went to the toilet, heard screaming not even 2 mins later. I ran in to see my grandma had fell off the toilet and somehow her granny panties got stuck and she had a wedgie! Weird designed toilets! They need to change them.
reviews.author: Maddie Rose

reviews.text: My mammy is 84 with dementia and has been here since June 3rd 2025... its been the best thing for her (and us, we don'tworryas much)..... The staff are simply the most caring and lovely people...  100%
reviews.author: Issy (Issy)

reviews.text: My mum was a resident at Westgate for 2.2 years. She had advanced Alzheimer Dementia - she was unable to communicate. I had quite a few issues regarding my mums care at Westgate that I feel others should know about. When my mum arrived she was on the first floor and was left for extended periods of time in bed. She could only come out of bed by borrowing someone elses wheelchair. It took well over a year for her to be assessed and consequently acquire her own wheelchair by which time she had moved to the ground floor dementia area. She had the same breakfast every day for 2.2 years - there was no variation. She was on quite a few occasions fed the same meal e.g. chicken for lunch and for dinner (this happened a lot). She was also fed curry again and again despite numerous conversations - had my mum the capacity to chose she would not have chosen curry (as she did not like spicy food). I completed a likes and disliked form when she arrived which was never followed. On one occasion she was fed mashed potato for lunch and not one member of the care staff questioned it - I’d turned up while the food was being distributed - I was mortified - bear in mind my mum was severly malnourished - not helped by a plate of mashed potato. I had to constantly ask for the wellbeing charts as they were not kept in her room until a few months before she passed away and then they changed from a weekly chart to a daily chart - so you had to ask to see the history - this took away precious time with my mum because I had to run around checking/finding the charts. But I think the worse thing was that they forged the wellbeing charts - on 2 occasions (I feel that this may have happened more times - as this happened on the first floor and the ground floor by 2 different carers - they had written that she was in bed e.g. 12 noon and I had just arrived and it was 11.20am - so they had no intention of doing a 12 noon check - this is unforgivable. I raised this with the manager who asked the carer to apologise personally. BTW - these two incidences covered two different Managers duration at Westgate. It was after this first event that I began to scrutinise the wellbeing charts as I had completely lost trust in them. Her water jug was never accessible and she was unable to say I’m thirsty’ - when I visited and gave her a drink - she drank a lot as she was obviously thirsty. I found her one day in her wheelchair (not strapped in) in the day room while everyone else was doing an activity in another part of the home. She also had unexplained bruising and skin tears. The last safe guarding incident was never resolved despite numerous attempts for an explanation - the care home would not give an explanation and social services never contacted me. If you care about your loved one - check the charts as things aren’t always what they seem. On a positive note - the rooms were nice and comfortable. I can assure that this account of Westgate is accurate.
reviews.author: carole gregory
